idea: Subscription library of generalist sector primers
buyer: Generalist analysts and PMs picking up unfamiliar sectors
pain: Getting up to speed on a new sector takes three days every time
v1: Six primers, sold as a growing library
verdict: Genuine leverage and a compounding asset, but the seat price cannot reach the target from her network alone.

why.distribution: Her exact peer group, reachable directly, though seats are an individual rather than firm purchase.
why.demand: The pain is inferred from her own experience and is a good inference; no external buyer has confirmed it.
why.fmf: Going from zero to a defensible sector view in days is precisely her rarest trained skill.
why.revenue_structure: Monthly subscription; the library growing gives a reason to stay.
why.defensibility: The back catalogue compounds and takes years to reproduce, though an LLM erodes the value of any single primer.
why.leverage: Pure media economics - one primer serves every subscriber forever.
why.time_to_revenue: Needs a credible starting library before anyone pays: 3-6 months.
why.tailwind: Adverse - a generalist model now produces a passable primer on demand.
why.ceiling: £300/mo x 55 seats = £198k, and 55 individual paying seats is far beyond a 50-person warm network.

ceiling_arithmetic: £300/mo x 55 seats = £198k. Her warm network is ~50 people and not all buy, so 55 paying seats requires reaching well beyond it. Realistic: 15-20 seats = £54-72k.
carries: The best leverage-to-effort ratio in the research cluster, and a genuinely compounding asset.
kills: Ceiling arithmetic. At £300/seat the volume required exceeds her reachable network, and AI has made the underlying artefact cheap.
test: Ask ten analysts what they would pay for a library of 30 primers.
test_pass: Several name a number at or above £300 and ask when.
test_fail: They say they would just ask an AI.
